command:change=$(find openspec/changes -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 -type d ! -name archive)
review="$change/review-code.md"
added=$(git log --diff-filter=A --format=%H -- "$review" | tail -1)
base=HEAD
[ -z "$added" ] || base="$added^"
touched=$({ git diff --name-only "$base"; git ls-files -o --exclude-standard; } | sort -u | grep -vxF "$review" | grep -v '^\.gnomish-task/' || true)
[ -z "$touched" ] || { echo "$touched"; echo "the review-code stage writes nothing but $review - restore the files above with: git checkout $base -- <file>"; exit 1; }

findings.message: Severity/Verdict: task 5.3 is ticked `[x]` in tasks.md:39, and the review itself marks it ❌ because the specified command crashes ('Test runner crashed … TypeError: Cannot convert object to primitive value'). Per acceptance, CRITICAL covers 'a ticked-but-undone task', yet R2 is a WARNING and the Verdict says 'Ready. There is no CRITICAL finding'. R2 should be CRITICAL and the Verdict not Ready.

R2 Fix contradicts the specs: it narrows the jq filter to work-bound scenario names. M3 asks only that each cache-hit mutant 'is killed by at least one test under `src/test/features/`', and design D7 fails only 'if a mutant's `killedBy` names no test from a file under `src/test/features/`'. The review's own per-file --disableBail run credits the bypass mutant to 'the device time zone FR2 `When` step', which is under src/test/features/, so M3 as written is met. The Fix risk admits the narrowed filter 'will likely print `false`', leaving 5.3 open for good against a bar no spec sets. A correct fix keeps the D7/M3 filter, runs it per file with --disableBail (the form the review found completes) and records the result.

Coverage inconsistency: tasks 3.1, 3.3 and 4.3 are marked ✅ while each line says 'The size check fails', and R1 says 'The tasks were ticked although the size check they include fails'. The group-3 routine in tasks.md requires 'check with `wc -l` that every touched steps or world file stays at most 300 lines and, where it already was, at most 200'. Since that check fails (255, 225, 204 lines, confirmed), these lines cannot carry ✅ unflagged; mark them ❌ or state the inconsistency.

Minor (does not fail the round on its own): locations_device_time_zone_unit.steps.tsx:155 has only `// @mark-device-time-zone-in-location-list @NFR-P1` and lacks the `// @replace-wall-clock-row-budgets-with-deterministic-checks @FR2` comment that every other touched steps file has. bdd-unit.md Key Rule 5 says 'Tag comment — before `f.Scenario` add comment `// @<change-name> @FR-X`'. The FR2 Requirements line does not mention the gap.

findings.message: R1 Fix contradicts its own Fix risk. Fix step 3 says to move the device time zone per-zone formatter assertion 'into `rowBudgetWorld.ts`', and step 2 offers `trackBudgetWorld.ts`. But the Fix risk says new helpers that call `expect` 'should go into separate check files … not into the worlds the benchmarks import'. Both worlds are imported by benchmarks (`rowPresenting.bench.ts:16`, `timeSelection.bench.ts:3`). Step 3 also targets a world that `locations_device_time_zone_unit.steps.tsx` does not import (it uses `./deviceTimeZoneWorld`, lines 13-18). Give one consistent target per move, e.g. a new check file per step file, shaped like `trackLabelsCheck.ts`.

R1 Fix risk misstates the existing code. It implies the benchmark-imported worlds hold no assertion code, but `rowBudgetWorld.ts:3` already imports `expect` from vitest and defines `expectNoWarmWork` (:48-51). `trackBudgetWorld.ts:2` imports `expect` and defines `expectEveryHandleAt`/`expectEveryTrackForDayStarting` (:81-103). The acceptance criteria require the Fix risk to be stated honestly, 'including what the existing code already does around it'.

R1 Fix cannot reach its own target ('`wc -l` them: each must print at most 200'). `locations_local_time_unit.steps.tsx` is 255 lines. Moving only the label comparison (lines 230-251, about 22 lines, plus about 4 import lines) leaves about 230. `time_selection_day_track.steps.tsx` is 225 lines. Moving the per-zone lookup loop (:170-175) and the `previousMoment` setup (:193-197) saves about 11 lines and leaves about 214. The Fix must name moves that actually bring each file to 200 or less (e.g. the whole label scenario's When/Then handlers and the budget Given/When setup into helpers), or give the line arithmetic.
